data.title: Hammond Power Solutions Declares Quarterly Dividend
data.description:
GUELPH, Ontario, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- (TSX: HPS.A) The Board of Directors of Hammond Power Solutions Inc. (“HPS”) declared a quarterly cash dividend of twenty-nine cents ($0.29) per Class A Subordinate Voting Share of HPS and a quarterly cash dividend of twenty-nine cents ($0.29) per Class B Common Share of HPS. The dividend will be payable on December 18, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on December 11, 2026. The ex-dividend date is December 11, 2026.

HPS designates the entire amount of this taxable dividend to be an “eligible dividend” for purposes of the Income Tax Act (Canada), as amended from time to time. data.title: CF Energy Announces Financial Results For the Three-Month and Nine-Month Periods Ended September 30, 2026
data.description:
TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / CF Energy Corp. (TSXV:CFY) ("CF Energy" or the "Company", together with its subsidiaries, the "Group"), an energy provider in the People's Republic of China (the "PRC" or "China"), announces that the Company has filed its unaudited interim consolidated financial results for the three-month and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026.

The unaudited interim consolidated financial statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis ("MD&A") can be downloaded from www.sedarplus.com or from the Company's website at www.cfenergy.com.

The unaudited interim consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board ("IASB") (collectively, "IFRS Accounting Standards"). This news release contains financial terms that are non-IFRS Accounting Standards ("non-GAAP") financial measures.

Results for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026 ("Q3 2026")

Continuing Operations

Gross Profit Margin 29.9% 31.0% -1.1%
Net Profit 3.2 3.8 (0.6) -17% 0.6 0.7 (0.1)

Revenue in Q3 2026 was RMB103.5 million (approx. CAD21.0 million), an increase of RMB14.9 million (approx. CAD3.8 million), or 17%, from RMB88.6 million (approx. CAD17.2 million) for the three months ended September 30, 2025 ("Q3 2025").

The increase in overall revenue in Q3 2026 was mainly attributed to the increase in revenue from residential customers of gas distribution utility sector. The positive effect of Hainan Free Port's opening-up policy continued to lead to an increase in both sales volume of gas supply to residential customers and the pipeline installation and connection revenue from residential customers since the first quarter of 2026 which carried through to Q3 2026.

The increase in installation pipeline revenue for new customers of the Haitang Bay Smart Energy project in the integrated smart energy segment also contributed to the increase in revenue in Q3 2026.

Gross profit in Q3 2026 was RMB30.9 million (approx. CAD6.3 million), an increase of RMB3.5 million (CAD1.0 million) or 13% from RMB27.4 million (approx. CAD5.3 million) in Q3 2025. Overall gross margin in Q3 2026 was 29.9%, a decrease of 1.1 percentage points from 31.0% in Q3 2025.

The overall decrease in gross profit margin in Q3 2026 as compared to Q3 2025 was mainly attributable to the offsetting effect of the benefit of reducing costs due to the centralization of procurement of materials for pipeline installation connection projects and the increase in unit price of pipeline installation and connection for residential customers by providing auxiliary services at minimal cost which partially offset the overall increase in material cost and labor cost since late December 2025, together with the increase of 3% in the purchase price of pipeline gas as compared to Q3 2025.

Net profit in Q3 2026 was RMB3.2 million (approx. CAD0.6 million), a decrease of RMB0.6 million (CAD0.1 million) or 17% from RMB3.8 million (approx. CAD0.7 million) in Q3 2025.

EBITDA (non-GAAP) in Q3 2026 was RMB22.2 million (approx. CAD4.5 million), a decrease of RMB1.0 million (approx. CAD0.0 million), or 4%, from RMB23.2 million (approx. CAD4.5 million) in Q3 2025.

Both basic and diluted earnings per share ("EPS") in Q3 2026 from continuing operations was RMB0.08 (CAD0.02) per share, an increase of RMB0.01 (CAD0.01), as compared to RMB0.07 CAD0.01) per share in Q3 2025.

The increase in overall revenue for the Nine Months in 2026 was attributed to the increase in revenue in Q3 2026 as mentioned above but offset by the decrease in the EV battery swap revenue in the smart mobility segment which was caused by a trend in switching of travel habits by tourists from taking taxis to renting Uber services when travelling in the Sanya City.

Gross profit for the Nine Months in 2026 was RMB87.2 million (approx. CAD17.7 million), an increase of RMB9.6 million (CAD2.7 million) or 12% from RMB77.6 million (approx. CAD15.0 million) for the Nine Months in 2025. Overall gross margin for the Nine Months in 2026 was 27.0%, an increase of 0.4 percentage points from 26.6% for the Nine Months in 2025.

A non-recurring urban gas pipeline facility renovation projects in 2024-2025 were agreed at relatively competitive prices with very low gross margin which had a dilutive effect on the overall gross profit and margin for the Nine Months in 2025. Excluding this dilutive effect, the gross profit margin for the Nine Months in 2026 and 2025 remained the same at 27.0% on a comparable basis.

Net profit for the Nine Months in 2026 was RMB8.8 million (approx. CAD1.8 million), an increase of RMB2.4 million (CAD0.6 million) or 37% from RMB6.4 million (approx. CAD1.2 million) for the Nine Months in 2025.

EBITDA (non-GAAP) for the Nine Months in 2026 was RMB65.5 million (approx. CAD13.3 million), a decrease of RMB0.7 million (approx. CAD0.5 million), or 1%, from RMB66.2 million (approx. CAD12.8 million) for the Nine Months in 2025.

Both basic and diluted earnings per share ("EPS") from continuing operations was RMB0.20 (CAD0.04) per share for the Nine Months in 2026, an increase of RMB0.04 (CAD0.01) as compared to RMB0.16 (CAD0.03) per share for the Nine Months in 2025.

Company Outlook

The global energy landscape is undergoing a fundamental transformation with accelerating efforts in electrification and digitalization of the industry. In the short-term, the global energy markets will remain volatile due to geopolitical uncertainties and supply chain disruptions while demand for electricity consumption continues to rise driven by the rapid growth of data centers, artificial intelligence applications and etc. The natural gas industry faces a variety of challenges ranging from regulatory impacts to market dynamics, but it continues to play a critical role as a transition fuel, supporting the integration of renewable energy, distributed energy resources, and digital energy management systems as they are becoming key components of modern energy infrastructure.

At the same time, the continued development of the Hainan Free Trade Port has significantly enhanced the economic vitality of the region, particularly in Sanya. The increase in tourism and commercial activity has driven higher for energy consumption, which also led to steady growth in the Company's natural gas supply business. The Company envisions that Sanya will expand its infrastructure including hospitality, retail, and transportation which will create additional opportunities for energy consumption and integrated energy services.

Distributed Smart Energy Ecosystem - Progress to Date:

CF Energy has continued its strategic transformation from a traditional natural gas company into a comprehensive energy solutions provider, focusing on incorporating its smart energy system and energy storage technology to create a highly integrated and efficient framework for sustainable energy management.

CF Energy's Haitang Bay integrated smart energy project and Meishan project are flagships of standalone distributed energy system with advanced grid technologies that enable real-time monitoring and responsive energy distribution based on demand and supply conditions. The Haitang Bay integrated smart energy system has enhanced energy efficiency and system flexibility through the application of ice storage for peak load shifting.

In parallel, the Company has entered the field of electrochemical energy storage for cost reduction and energy conservation through the mode of battery swapping in new energy vehicles. The battery swap station network in Sanya and Beihai have been contributing to the optimization of the power grid as they reduce strain on the electrical grid and avoid demand spikes.

Distributed Smart Energy Ecosystem -Current Initiatives:

The Company is working with partners in the IoT (internet of things), and cloud services field to create an efficient EMS (energy management system) that connects the standalone distributed smart energy systems with various energy management and storage technologies. This will serve as the core infrastructure for enabling virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities. Through the deployment of IoT-enabled devices and data acquisition systems, the Company will be able to collect real-time data on energy production, storage levels, battery health, and consumption patterns. Using historical data and machine learning models, the EMS can predict demand spikes, potential system disruptions, and optimal energy production schedules. This will form the operational backbone of the Company's virtual power plant strategy.

Distributed Smart Energy Ecosystem - Outlook and Strategic Direction:

The Company will continue its development in energy management driven by electrification, increasing renewable penetration, and rising demand for power grid stability. The Company aims to aggregate and optimize the distributed energy assets including centralized cooling system, battery swap stations, and energy storage system into a platform which enables the development of virtual power plant with active end user participation. This will provide support in power grid stability via peak shaving, load balancing, and frequency regulation.

In addition, the Company is working to integrate a demand response system where hotels and other end users can opt-in to adjust their energy usage during peak periods in response to incentives. For example, shifting non-essential power usage to off-peak hours. EV owners can charge their vehicles during off-peak hours to benefit from lower rates and reduce grid strain during high-demand periods. Alternatively, V2G (Vehicle to Grid) concept allows EVs to return energy to the grid during peak times, effectively using the vehicle's battery as a grid resource. Furthermore, utilizing a platform for energy trading that allows surplus energy (from renewable sources and stored energy) to be sold back to the grid or shared among participants will add additional revenue stream and encouraging sustainable practices. The integration must connect all components through a smart grid that enables two-way communication between the energy providers and consumers.

About CF Energy Corp. (Previously known as: Changfeng Energy Inc.)

CF Energy Corp. is a Canadian public company currently traded on the Toronto Venture Exchange ("TSX-V") under the stock symbol "CFY". It is an integrated energy provider and natural gas distribution company (or natural gas utility) in the PRC. CF Energy strives to combine leading clean energy technology with natural gas usage to provide sustainable energy to its customer base in the PRC.

data.title: 'I've been a stay-at-home mom': I'm 50 and have a chronic illness. My husband lost his job. Should he raid his 401(k)?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Our financial and healthcare situation has become increasingly concerning'

"COBRA is too expensive. I also looked into Priority Health coverage and was quoted $1,400 per month, which is beyond what we can manage financially." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I am 50, and my husband recently lost his job. I have been a stay-at-home mom for many years and also live with a chronic illness that limits my ability to work full-time. I recently started working as a daycare aide at our local public school, but our financial and healthcare situation has become increasingly concerning.

I have several questions:

1. Health insurance and access to medical care

Unfortunately, my husband was not transparent with me about the circumstances surrounding his employment, so I wasn't given the opportunity to plan ahead for my healthcare needs. My health insurance was tied to his employment and, as a result, I was unable to renew my specialty medications or schedule an appointment with my neurologist.

COBRA is too expensive. I also looked into Priority Health coverage and was quoted $1,400 per month, which is beyond what we can manage. What other options should I explore? Are there affordable health insurance alternatives, marketplace plans, or assistance programs that could help someone in my situation?

2. My husband's 401(k) and retirement savings

My husband is considering withdrawing money from his 401(k). These funds are intended to support us during retirement. What is the best way to handle his 401(k)? Would rolling it over into an IRA or another retirement account be a better option than withdrawing the money? Are there ways to transfer or invest these funds without triggering unnecessary taxes?

3. My personal savings and retirement planning

I have $150,000 in a money-market account earning 3.1% interest. This money represents savings from my previous employment, along with funds I consistently set aside from our monthly household budget over the years. I want to make sure I am being responsible with this money and putting it to work for my future.

What would be the best way to manage these savings for retirement? Should I keep the money in a money-market account, consider CDs or high-yield savings accounts, or explore other investment options that could provide better long-term growth while protecting my principal? I need to make informed decisions and protect my financial future.

Feeling Insecure

Related: 'I have no financial safety net': I'm 66, rely on Social Security and have just $500 in savings. What hope do I have?

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually. Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group.

He can apply for insurance outside the normal open-enrollment period from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027, on the ACA Marketplace.

Dear Insecure,

Your healthcare plan is an immediate priority, so sort that out ASAP.

Losing workplace health insurance qualifies your husband for a special enrollment period on healthcare.gov. He has a 60-day window after the loss of his coverage to pick a plan. The ACA Marketplace may ask for documents, including an employer or insurer notice, to verify when his coverage ends. The ACA Marketplace calculates his premium based on his age, location, household size and expected household income for the entire calendar year.

Importantly, he can apply outside the normal open-enrollment period, which runs from Nov. 1, 2026, through Jan. 15, 2027, on the ACA Marketplace. He may also qualify for an ACA subsidy. If he was earning $45,000 before being laid off and, assuming he doesn't have another job to go to, he will earn less for the remainder of the year; he will need to estimate his total income for 2026, which includes his salary up until the time he was laid off and unemployment benefits.

There is no asset test for most adults under 65 who qualify for the ACA Marketplace through the rules based on their modified adjusted gross income (MAGI). MAGI is calculated using adjusted gross income, taking certain adjustments or deductions into account. It's used to determine eligibility for certain tax deductions and credits, as well as certain government benefits and surcharges. The formula can change depending on what benefits you are applying for.

It's not so unusual to get sticker shock from COBRA's prices.

If your husband applies through the ACA Marketplace and his income appears low enough for Medicaid rather than Marketplace subsidies, the application should probably be referred to the relevant state program. Given that he has just lost his job and his income has dropped, tell him to check both state healthcare plans and ACA Marketplace plans. As you point out, it's not so unusual to get sticker shock from COBRA's prices.

COBRA can cost $800 a month for individual coverage and $2,300 for family coverage, depending on the plan. Again, he has 60 days to elect COBRA, and once he pays the required premiums, his coverage can be applied retroactively to when his employer coverage ended. To qualify for COBRA, the U.S. Labor Department says he must have been covered by his employer's group health plan, the plan must be subject to COBRA, and other qualifying conditions must be met.

Some Moneyist Facebook Group members weighed in on your questions. "Don't get distracted with things that don't matter," one wrote. "Rolling over your husband's 401(k) is not a priority. It can stay in his employer's custodian and roll over to a Schwab or Fidelity-type institution when things calm down. His focus needs to be 100% on getting a new job, not worrying about your retirement. You are nowhere near ready for retirement so employment is what matters."

Don't miss: 'It leaves me with a sour taste': My elderly mother gave our cousin $800 for a car repair. Should I be worried?

Retirement savings and planning

I understand why you and your husband might think withdrawing from your 401(k) could help, but it could have the opposite effect in the long run. I urge you to proceed cautiously. There's increasing evidence that, with the rising cost of living and stubbornly high interest rates, more Americans feel under pressure to dip into their retirement savings - sometimes as a short-term loan, which they may not be able to pay back.

If your husband does dip into his 401(k), he may be forced to pay a 10% penalty for withdrawing funds before 591/2 and, if that wasn't harsh enough, he will also be required to pay income tax on his early withdrawal. For example, if you need $50,000 to supplement your living expenses over the next 12 months, he may need to withdraw considerably more to account for taxes and potential penalties. The IRS has effectively made every effort to deter you from doing so.

There is a "rule of 55" for making unexpected or early withdrawals. If a person leaves or loses their job during or after the calendar year they turn 55, or age 50 for certain public-safety workers, they can make withdrawals from a 401(k) plan without having to pay that 10% penalty. Income taxes still apply, however, and the funds must remain in that employer's 401(k) rather than being rolled over to an IRA.

We are living in a "low fire, low hire" jobs environment.

Given your age, investing your $150,000 in a diversified stock-market portfolio could make more sense than a money-market account, high-yield savings account (HYSA) or CD. Keeping it in a money-market account (at a 3.1% interest rate) could give you around $203,500 over 10 years versus $222,000 in a HYSA or CD (at 4%), or $295,000 in a balanced portfolio (at 7%). The big caveat is that the stock market provides no guarantees.

There are no hard-and-fast rules, but many advisers recommend that someone around 50 consider an asset allocation of 60% to 80% equities and 20% to 40% fixed income (bonds and cash equivalents). However, your risk tolerance plays a big part in that. It would not be unusual to find someone who is invested in 90% or even, in some cases, 100% stocks at 50, given that they have another 15 years or more until they retire.

In the meantime, cut your costs and look into selling any valuables that could get you through this financial crunch. I trust your husband has applied for unemployment insurance and has pursued your health-insurance options before that 60-day window has closed. You will need patience. We are living in a "low fire, low hire" jobs environment. The average job search takes about three to six months, so be prepared for a hard slog.

Keep your cool and don't make any hasty decisions.

Related: My 93-year-old father changed his will at the 11th hour, leaving my brother his entire $500,000 estate. Can I challenge it?

data.title: MINILUXE REPORTS THIRD QUARTER AND YEAR-TO-DATE FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR THE 13 AND 39 WEEKS ENDED SEPTEMBER 27, 2026
data.description:
Net Revenue Up 6% in the Third Quarter; System Sales Exceed $8M in a Quarter; Company Makes Multiple Growth Investments in Q3, Including New Studio Opening and Acquisition

All reported figures in U.S. Dollars unless otherwise noted

Boston, MA, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MiniLuxe Holding Corp. (TSXV: MNLX) today announced its financial results for the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 27, 2026 (“Q3 2026” and “YTD 2026”, respectively). The comparative prior year periods are the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 28, 2025.

MiniLuxe is on a mission to make self-care something you can feel good about, starting with your nails. The Company delivers premium nail care in studios known for hospital-grade hygiene, cleaner polishes, and treatments that are better for you and for the people who provide them. What sets MiniLuxe apart is its people and culture, which are at the center of its competitive advantage. In an industry infamous for churn and poor working conditions, MiniLuxe has retained 86% of its hourly workforce on average over each of the last three years. Team members who are with the Company five years or more receive stock options, giving them a stake in the Company’s success, along with real career paths. Today, more than half of MiniLuxe’s service professionals (nail designers and waxing specialists) have reached that milestone.

The third quarter of 2026 delivered another quarter of year-over-year growth, with total Company net revenue up 6.1% to $7.7M and system sales up 8% to $8.1M from $7.5M in Q3 2025. Growth was driven by continued same-studio sales gains in both volume and mix. System sales include sales from all MiniLuxe studios, including franchised locations. The quarter extends a long, unbroken run of year-over-year revenue growth, reflecting continued demand for MiniLuxe services.

The Company made multiple growth investments in the third quarter: new studios, new AI-driven, geo-targeted paid marketing tests, upgrades to existing studios, and additional nail designer hours ahead of the fourth-quarter holiday season, its period of peak demand. While these initiatives resulted in some short-term margin pullback, management expects them to deliver meaningful returns over the longer term. After the quarter ended, the Company also put in place its first price increase in approximately three years, of approximately 5%, which management expects to more than offset rising labor and health care benefit costs.

  • New studios: The Company opened its Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio on July 30 and acquired a majority interest in an existing studio in Burlington, Massachusetts on September 4. The third quarter was also the first full quarter for the new MiniLuxe Lakewood studio in Dallas.
  • Marketing tests: Early results are encouraging, with some test studios attracting record numbers of new clients who are also returning faster for repeat visits.
  • Studio upgrades: The Company began renovating several existing studios with new dual stations that allow a manicure and pedicure at the same time. In the first studios, these stations cost at least 50% less than legacy stations, and productivity per station has been as much as double that of legacy pedicure stations.
  • Nail designer hours: Staffed hours were up 7% over the prior year, which positions the Company well for fourth-quarter demand.

 MiniLuxe’s Focus and Key Strategic Pillars in Q3 2026

The Company continued to make meaningful progress across each of its core strategic pillars in the third quarter of fiscal 2026:

  1. Attract, develop and retain high-quality nail designer talent;
  2. Drive growth through operating partners and franchise partners;
  3. Accelerate overall studio-level profitability and drive overall Company profitability;
  4. Strengthen balance sheet with sufficient capital to execute against growth plans.

Highlights of Business Performance

  • Total Company net revenue grew 6.1% to $7.7M in Q3 2026 from $7.3M in Q3 2025, bringing year-to-date revenue to $21.8M, up 4.3% from $20.9M in YTD 2025.

  • General and administrative expense was $3.82M in Q3 2026 versus $3.60M in Q3 2025, an increase of 6.0%, primarily reflecting spend toward growth initiatives, including marketing tests and new studio openings. As a percentage of net revenue, G&A was flat year over year at approximately 49.6%. Year to date, G&A was $11.10M versus $10.90M in YTD 2025, up 1.9%, and declined to 51.0% of net revenue from 52.2%.
  • Operating loss was ($1.59M) in Q3 2026 versus ($1.26M) in Q3 2025, reflecting the growth investments described above; YTD operating loss was essentially flat at ($4.47M) versus ($4.45M) in YTD 2025.
  • Full Company Adjusted EBITDA was ($1.57M) in Q3 2026 versus ($0.89M) in Q3 2025, and ($4.23M) for YTD 2026 versus ($3.34M) for YTD 2025. Most of the change was driven by the timing of expenses and one-time items. Excluding one-time items, management estimates Normalized Adjusted EBITDA of ($1.27M) in the quarter, compared with ($1.02M) in Q3 2025.
  • During the third quarter, the Company issued 1,428,571 Class A Subordinate Voting Shares at a deemed price of $0.35 per share in settlement of a $500,000 third-party obligation (the gift-card holdback from the Paintbox acquisition).
  • At the end of Q3 2026 (September 27, 2026), cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $4.5M (Q2 2026: $6.1M; year-end 2025: $4.5M), and working capital was positive at $0.2M.

The Company continued to expand through operating partners and franchise partners. Overall gross franchise sales were up 53% in the third quarter and 102% year to date.  The Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio opened on July 30, 2026, the Lakewood (Dallas) studio reopened as a MiniLuxe studio on June 5, 2026, and the Burlington, Massachusetts studio, acquired September 4, 2026, is operated through a 51%-owned limited liability company with its existing owner as operating partner.

Management Commentary

“In Q3, we continued to grow revenue year over year and expanded our studio footprint, with new studio openings and new locations in development. We also increased total nail designer hours and put marketing tests in place to attract new customers. We are already seeing early results as we attract new customers and see repeat visits, and we believe these investments will deliver a significant return over the medium to longer term. One of the most noteworthy statistics for me is that about half of our customer base is now Gen Z, which bodes well for the longevity of our brand and customer lifetime value.” – Tony Tjan, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

Other Developments

  • Substantial Issuer Bid (SIB). The Company’s SIB for up to C$6.0 million of its Class A Subordinate Voting Shares expired at 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on September 24, 2026. No Subordinate Voting Shares were purchased under the offer and all tendered shares were returned to shareholders.
  • Paintbox New York studio. On September 7, 2026, the Company closed its “store-in-store” Paintbox studio in New York, New York. The Company had a short-term arrangement with a hair studio to use its space as a “store-in-store” concept, and the arrangement was not extended.
  • Acquisition of Belle Vista Nail Studio. On September 4, 2026, the Company formed MNLX Burlington JV LLC and acquired the assets of Belle Vista Nail Studio in Burlington, Massachusetts for cash consideration of approximately $0.3M, issuing a 49% interest in the new company to the sellers. MiniLuxe will convert this studio to its own brand in 2027.

The Company continues to evaluate accretive M&A opportunities and is in discussions with several nail studio operators that it believes fit its purpose of empowering nail designers, and where it can create shared value by applying MiniLuxe’s brand standards and back-office infrastructure.

Non-IFRS Measures and Reconciliation of Non-IFRS Measures

This press release references certain non-IFRS measures used by management. These measures are not recognized under International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”), do not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS, and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. Rather, these measures are provided as additional information to complement those IFRS measures by providing further understanding of the Company’s results of operations from management’s perspective. Accordingly, these measures should not be considered in isolation nor as a substitute for analysis of the Company’s financial information reported under IFRS. The non-IFRS measures referred to in this press release are “Adjusted EBITDA”, “Normalized Adjusted EBITDA”, and system sales.

Adjusted EBITDA

Management believes Adjusted EBITDA most accurately reflects the commercial reality of the Company’s operations on an ongoing basis by adding back non-cash expenses. Additionally, the rent-related adjustments ensure that studio-related expenses align with revenue generated over the corresponding time periods.

Adjusted EBITDA is calculated by adding back fixed asset depreciation, right-of-use asset amortization under IFRS 16, asset disposal, and share-based compensation expense to IFRS operating income, then deducting cash rent expenses net of lease abatements. When relevant, we will add back adjustments made to the P&L as a result of accounting policies that are non-cash or do not have operational impacts (for example, inventory adjustments or deferred revenue). IFRS operating income is revenue less cost of sales (gross profit), additionally adjusted for general and administrative expenses, and depreciation and amortization expenses. Normalized Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA, further adjusted to (i) remove items that management considers one-time or not representative of ongoing operations, and (ii) present the comparative period on a basis consistent with the current period. Management uses Normalized Adjusted EBITDA to assess the Company’s run-rate operating performance. It should be read together with, and not as a substitute for, operating loss and Adjusted EBITDA.

About MiniLuxe

MiniLuxe Holding Corp. is a Boston-based lifestyle brand and talent empowerment platform transforming the fragmented beauty and self-care industry through its premium service brand, proprietary products, and operating platform. For more than 15 years, MiniLuxe has delivered high-quality nail care, waxing, and esthetic services through a growing network of company-owned, joint venture, and partner-operated studios, completing more than 5 million services to date.

The Company is recognized for its elevated service experience, rigorous hygiene standards, non-toxic products, modern studio design, and commitment to socially responsible labor practices. MiniLuxe’s differentiated model is designed to create better outcomes for both clients and beauty professionals through career development, economic mobility, equity participation, and future ownership opportunities.

MiniLuxe is expanding its reach through a multi-pronged growth strategy that includes new studio development, franchising, and the acquisition and conversion of existing nail studios. By combining a trusted consumer brand, proprietary products, operating expertise, and technology-enabled systems, the Company offers entrepreneurs and operators the opportunity to partner with a proven platform while preserving a strong focus on talent development and service excellence.

Through its growing studio network and product portfolio, MiniLuxe seeks to build the leading trusted brand in beauty and self-care while generating long-term value for clients, talent, and shareholders.

data.title: I'm terrified of a market crash. Should I put $400,000 of my $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have a house worth $450,000. Our combined annual income is $125,000.'

"We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm wondering what your thoughts are on putting our house and other assets into a trust. Could it help reduce taxes or protect our assets from lawsuits, bankruptcy or other unforeseen circumstances? If so, what are the potential downsides or pitfalls?

We have a house worth $450,000 and about $1 million in retirement assets held in various qualified accounts. I'd also be interested in your thoughts on annuities for capital preservation and guaranteed income.

Would it make sense to put $400,000 of our $1 million in qualified retirement accounts into an annuity that would begin paying out at age 65, guaranteeing us $40,000 a year for life, while leaving the remaining $600,000 invested in a brokerage account for capital appreciation?

My spouse and I are 55 and 54, respectively. We're both working and plan to continue until 65. We're terrified of a market crash. We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000.

Curious in the Midwest

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'Nvidia has me spooked ': Should I sell my stocks or buy real estate?

That money you invest in an annuity is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Dear Curious,

I'll outline the advantages of your proposal - and then move on to the cons.

First, the pros of putting your money in an annuity, I presume, are to find a haven for part of your nest egg, albeit at a potentially lower rate than the stock market could provide. If you moved $400,000 from traditional 401(k)s or IRAs into an IRA annuity, the transaction generally would not trigger income taxes or the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, provided the funds are transferred correctly. A direct trustee-to-trustee transfer is typically the simplest approach. If you were selling $400,000 worth of investments in an ordinary brokerage account, however, you could owe capital-gains taxes on any profits realized from the sale.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security, which you presumably plan to take when you reach full retirement age. What you receive depends on the type of annuity: your initial investment, the interest rate or other terms you lock in and, of course, the payment schedule. Payouts can also vary with your age, your sex and whether the product is a joint-life annuity. If you expect to live a long time, a lifetime annuity can protect you from outliving your retirement savings. The trade-off is access: That money is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security.

An annuity is neither a bond nor cash. It works as an insurance contract: you pay an insurance company in exchange for income. An immediate annuity starts paying within a year of purchase, while a deferred annuity starts at a later date. Money in a 401(k) or IRA that is invested in stocks can grow over time and help keep pace with inflation. Annuity income is usually fixed, so it can lose purchasing power as prices rise unless you add an inflation adjustment or rider, but that protection also comes at a price: a lower initial payout. Annuity fees can be as much as 10% of the value of your contract. Surrender charges can be substantial if you withdraw money early.

But I have some questions: I understand why the prospect of $40,000 in guaranteed annual income is tempting. If payments continued for those periods, you would collect $400,000 over 10 years, $800,000 over 20 years and potentially $1.2 million over 30 years. Make sure you read the fine print. Is that $40,000 guaranteed income for one person's lifetime? Or is it for both of your lifetimes? Does the surviving spouse continue to receive the full $40,000-a-year income? Is there a death benefit or return-of-premium provision or rider if one spouse dies? Last but not least, are the $40,000-a-year payments adjusted for inflation?

Don't miss: My wife and I are in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage or invest in a stock market driven by AI?

Investing in the stock market

Third, the pros of leaving the money in the stock market: If you left your $400,000 invested for another 10 years instead of putting it into an annuity, it could grow to approximately $592,000 at an annual return of 4%, $787,000 at 7%, or $864,000 at 8%. These estimates assume annual compounding, with investment earnings reinvested, and exclude taxes, fees and additional contributions. The biggest difference between this scenario and the option of buying an annuity with your $400,000 is that the former is not guaranteed. You are potentially giving up the prospect of a larger return in exchange for security.

An annuity and a trust provide different estate-planning functions. Annuities distribute your assets per the terms of the contract, whereas a trust is designed to manage, protect and distribute your estate during your lifetime and beyond. As this guide on Estate Guru points out, trusts and annuities solve different estate-planning problems: (1) Bypassing probate or buying an annuity isn't an estate plan. (2) A trust can manage your assets if you become incapacitated, provide for minor children or beneficiaries with special needs, address the complications of a blended family and set out the conditions for an inheritance.

Revocable living trusts can benefit people with modest estates, particularly those seeking to avoid probate or plan for incapacity. For families with complicated estates, putting accounts and assets under a single trustee can keep everything running smoothly. It can also help prevent conflicts involving beneficiary designations. Marital trusts matter most in blended families, where each spouse wants to be sure their own children are provided for if the other dies. A special-needs trust can supplement government benefits, while a spendthrift trust can prevent beneficiaries from selling or using their future inheritance as collateral for a loan.

Know what you're buying, and be sure you're doing it for the right reasons.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

data.title: Marrelli Capital Limited and Salma and Noah Limited Partnership - Joint Early Warning News Release Regarding Common Shares of Longview Capital (No. 1) Inc.

TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Marrelli Capital Limited ("MCL"), an Ontario Corporation, and Salma and Noah Limited Partnership ("SNLP"),an Ontario limited partnership, announce that they have each filed an early warning report (each an "EWR" and collectively, the "EWRs") in respect of common shares ("Shares") of Longview Capital (No. 1) Inc. (formerly BE Resources Inc.) (the "Company").

On November 24, 2026, MCL sold an aggregate of 2,536,392 Shares, representing approximately 22.33% of the 11,357,940 issued and outstanding Shares, to SNLP for total consideration of C$19,998.00 (approximately C$0.0079 per Share) (the "Transaction"). The Transaction was a transfer between affiliated entities under common control. It was completed by private agreement and did not take place on any market. SNLP relied on the private agreement exemption in section 4.2 of National Instrument 62-104 Take-Over Bids and Issuer Bids. The Shares were purchased from one seller, MCL, by private agreement; the purchase was not made to securityholders of the Company generally; and there is no published market for the Shares.

Immediately prior to the Transaction, MCL held 2,536,392 Shares, representing approximately 22.33% of the issued and outstanding Shares, and SNLP held nil Shares. Immediately following the Transaction, SNLP holds 2,536,392 Shares, representing approximately 22.33% of the issued and outstanding Shares, and MCL holds nil Shares. MCL previously filed an early warning report dated July 6, 2026 in respect of the Shares, which MCL's EWR updates to reflect the Transaction.

SNLP acquired the Shares from MCL for investment purposes and as part of a reorganization of shareholdings among entities under common control. MCL, SNLP and their joint actors are aware that the Company has called an annual and special meeting of shareholders for December 18, 2026 to consider, among other things, the continuance of the Company from Ontario into British Columbia and the adoption of new articles, that the Company intends to relocate its head office to Vancouver, British Columbia following the continuance, and that its board of directors is evaluating a potential reorganization by way of a plan of arrangement under which shares of one or more newly incorporated subsidiaries of the Company would be distributed to shareholders, each as described in the Company's management information circular dated November 9, 2026. No agreement has been entered into in respect of the potential reorganization, its terms have not been settled, and there is no assurance that it will be proposed or completed.

Other than as described above, MCL, SNLP and their joint actors have no current plans or future intentions that relate to or would result in any of the matters described in Item 5 of Form 62-103F1. Depending on the Company's business and prospects and other factors, MCL, SNLP and their joint actors may in the future acquire additional securities of the Company, or dispose of some or all of the securities of the Company that they hold, by private agreement or otherwise, subject in each case to applicable securities laws.

The head office of the Company and the address of each of MCL and SNLP is located at 82 Richmond Street East, Toronto, Ontario M5C 1P1. Copies of the EWRs are available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and may also be obtained by contacting Marie-Josee Audet by email at maudet@marrellisupport.ca or by telephone at (416) 278-5519.

Forward-Looking Information
